name: sabihs-birdbrain
description: On-device bird sound identification PWA with a visual explanation of how the AI identifies each bird. BirdNET + TensorFlow.js.

paragraphs: Point your phone at the dawn chorus and see who is singing. Sabih’s Birdbrain is a progressive web app that identifies bird sounds in real time, entirely on the device, using the BirdNET V2.4 neural network running in TensorFlow.js inside a Web Worker. It records, re-analyses, explains its own identifications, looks species up, maps where you heard them, and works offline once installed.
Screenshots taken with Playwright at iPhone 13 size from the built app. The species page shows the retry state because the build machine’s shared network address was rate-limited by Wikipedia.
features: Listen: Start/Stop continuous listening, multi-species results with

confidences, confidence threshold slider, elapsed time, inference time, dropped-window count, screen wake lock (with a notice when unsupported), resume after returning to the foreground, a “Try the sample clip” demo,…
Microphone handling: asks the browser for raw audio (echo cancellation,

noise suppression and automatic gain off) and shows in Settings what was actually applied; a 150 Hz low-cut filter on the analysis path (default on) removes wind rumble from what the model hears while saved recordings…
Location filter: GPS plus BirdNET’s week-of-year (four per month) through
